investigations.name: eukaryogenesis
investigations.title: From Symbiosis to Complexity
investigations.question: Under what physical, metabolic, ecological, and evolutionary conditions can a symbiotic association between an archaeal host and a bacterial partner transition into an integrated eukaryotic cell? The aim is not to animate a predetermined history but to identify plausible, impossible, and still-unresolved pathways from ecological association to a new evolutionary individual.
investigations.hypothesis: Eukaryogenesis can be investigated as a succession of coupled transitions in ecological dependence, physical topology, energetic organization, and evolutionary individuality. Each transition introduces new benefits and new constraints; the discovery problem is which combinations of mechanisms allow cooperation to become stable cellular integration, and which competing histories remain consistent with the surviving evidence.

investigations.name: origins-of-life-vent
investigations.title: The Hydrothermal Vent Hypothesis
investigations.question: Could the first cells have originated at alkaline hydrothermal vents — and where does the geology-to-cells path run continuously, where does it depend on narrow regimes, and where does it break? Can a physically plausible early-Earth vent–ocean interface generate and sustain, in order, the free energy, reduced carbon, persistent network chemistry, concentration, and compartments a protocell needs — without inserting metabolism, membranes, autocatalysis, or heredity by assumption?
investigations.hypothesis: Under field- and lab-consistent parameter ranges, a serpentinization-fed, spatially resolved alkaline vent reproduces the conditions for a cellular origin: it crosses, in order, falsifiable thresholds for sustained carbon fixation, network persistence, concentration/individuality, compartmentation, internalized energy, and heritable organization — with identifiable parameter regions where each step fails.
